## Reconstruction-stage floors {#sec-ch08-reconfloors}

sources: OUTLINE.md 8.8

### Summary

A high-order reconstruction can overshoot into a negative face density or pressure even from a
perfectly admissible cell state. These floors catch that at the face, before the Riemann solver sees it.
They belong to the reconstruction framework of @sec-ch04-framework and are described here because they
are part of the positivity story rather than part of the interpolation.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Floors applied to the face states, not to the cell state, right after each reconstruction.
- Switch: the same limiter switch; the floor values come from the equation of state.
- Density and pressure take the floors; tracers are clamped at zero.
- The tracer clamp fires even when the caller asked for no floors, which the well-balanced path does.
:::

### Derivation

None: a floor is a clamp, and everything said about non-conservation in @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies
here too. Its check applies here too: `[C2]` measures the mass and energy a floor invents and finds
both strictly positive, because a clamp can only add [check `src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.py`,
output `src/snapy_report/ch08/floors_check.out`]. That is the shared property; the asymmetry below is
a branch structure, read from the code and not measured. What is worth recording is the asymmetry
between the three row groups, because it is not what a reader would guess.

Density and pressure are floored only when the caller asked for floors. Tracers are clamped at zero
whenever the limiter is on, *regardless* of what the caller asked, at
`clamp_min_` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}). The well-balanced path of @sec-ch05 calls the reconstruction with
floors switched off precisely so that it can handle its own perturbation variables, and it still gets
its tracers clamped.

### Numerical method

The three groups are floored in place as each is reconstructed: density at
`eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}), pressure at `eos` ({{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}) and the tracers
at {{< code src/recon/reconstruct.cpp ReconstructImpl::forward >}}. The values are read from the equation-of-state options and not
from the reconstruction options, which carry floor members that `forward` never reads.

### Tests

No test isolates the face floors. They fire inside every limited deck.

### Limits

1. **The tracer clamp ignores its caller.** A path that switches floors off to protect its own variables
   still has its tracer face states clamped. Whether that is intended is not recorded anywhere; the
   chapter records the behaviour.
2. **Same absolute values.** The face floors use the same absolute numbers as the cell floors, so the
   scaling caveat of @sec-ch08-eoslimiter applies to them unchanged.
